_readme: Promote-time constraints that must bite ON THE DAY SOMEBODY PROMOTES, not in prose.
Checked by tools/agent/promote_atoms.py (selfcheck leg 'promote-atoms'); exit 3 on violation.
rule 'no_promote_without': if any `subject` id is PROMOTED (no live gate site left) while any
`prereq` id is still GATED, the tree ships a configuration no wave has run -> RED.
An id named here that is neither gated nor marked promoted anywhere in the tree is also RED:
a typo in this file must never make a constraint quietly vacuous.
ADD A ROW the moment a constraint is ruled, not when it is about to be violated.

atoms.name: field_hold_needs_magnitude
subject: stayfield
stayfield2
atoms.direction: one-way: promoting fieldsip while the holding side stays gated is NOT constrained by this row.
note: ACCEPTED, with the premise re-founded on a bare reading rather than on the proposing
section's sentence. §ED.5 wrote '至今每一波给 stayfield/stayfield2 买 (a) 的波都同时 armed 了
fieldsip'. Measured this round by replaying each wave's own pinned tree
(`git show <W*_wave.json:tree>:iterations/streams/test_set.md` line 2, W24..W47):
W27..W47 co-arm all three, as claimed -- but W24, W25 and W26 armed stayfield+stayfield2
with fieldsip ABSENT from the armed string, and at W24's tree (2d1024ee) the
`IsSoakCandidate('fieldsip')` gate did not exist in bots/ at all (0 sites; 1 site from
b51bac77 on). An unarmed fieldsip makes J.IsFieldSipEnough return true early, which is
byte-identically the behaviour a REJECTED fieldsip would ship -> those three waves did run
the configuration §ED.5 calls untested. So the constraint stands on the narrower, true
footing: 21 of the last 24 waves co-armed them, and the only three that did not are old,
bundle-wide (42-44 armed ids), and not known to carry a per-id condition-(a) reading for
the holding side.
RELEASE CONDITION (what would retire this row): a condition-(a) reading for stayfield /
stayfield2 taken on W24, W25 or W26 -- or on any future leg where fieldsip is unarmed.
If such a reading exists and is usable, this row is over-strict and should be dropped;
until someone looks, promoting the holding side alone ships an unmeasured configuration.

atoms.name: tp_response_releases_need_commit
subject: tpdying
tpdead
atoms.direction: one-way: promoting tpcommit while either release stays gated is NOT constrained by this row.
note: REGISTERED BEFORE A VIOLATION, per this file's own README ('ADD A ROW the moment a
constraint is ruled'). Nothing is wrong with these two ids today: tpcommit is armed
alongside them, so both releases are reachable in every wave that carries them.
WHAT THE ROW STOPS is the promote-day configuration. Both gate sites live INSIDE
J.GetTpCommitDefendDesire (bots/FunLib/jmz_func.lua:8655), whose first statement is
`if not J.IsSoakCandidate('tpcommit') then return nil end` (:8657). Promote tpdying or
tpdead alone and the promoted code ships behind a gate that is OFF in every real game:
a promote that changes nothing, recorded as a shipped improvement. That is the same
family as GH #531 -- a lever whose reachability is decided by a DIFFERENT id -- and the
same family as the pullcad trap, one level up: pullcad freezes a predicate FALSE at
promote time, this ships a live predicate nobody can reach.
WHY IT WAS INVISIBLE UNTIL NOW: the dependency is structural NESTING, not a conjunction,
so no gate-reading tool sees it, and it was written down twice in prose -- the function's
own comments ('reachable only inside the tpcommit gate') and test_set.md:3625 ('挂在已
armed 的 tpcommit 下,可接受'). Prose is exactly what zusstatic was carrying when it sat
armed for a fortnight measuring nothing (§EX.3).
RELEASE CONDITION (what would retire this row): tpcommit promoted, or either release
lifted out of J.GetTpCommitDefendDesire so that it stands on its own gate.

atoms.name: static_field_needs_binding
subject: zusstatic
atoms.ref: iterations/streams/test_set.md §EX.3 / §EX.4 / §EX.5; GH #173 (the fact) / GH #531 (the SHAPE: a gate whose predicate is always TRUE while its answer is always 0, because the handle arrives through a parameter from a DIFFERENT id's gate)
atoms.direction: one-way: promoting zusbind while zusstatic stays gated is NOT constrained by this row.
note: REGISTERED IN THE SAME BREATH AS A RETURN-TO-SENDER, not before a violation.
zusstatic was armed 62/63-wide with zusbind absent from the armed string the whole time.
The dependency is REAL but it is not a conjunction, so no machine could see it: the gate at
bots/BotLib/hero_zuus.lua:619 sits in X.GetStaticFieldBonus(hAbility), and hAbility is a
PARAMETER handed in by the single call site at :652 through X.GetBoundAbility(...), which is
itself gated on zusbind. Unarmed, that layer short-circuits to `return hShipped` = the
file-local abilityAS = bot:GetAbilityByName(sAbilityList[5]).
tests/test_zuus_ability_index_binding.lua drives the SHIPPED J.Skill.GetAbilityList through
all 2^3 = 8 drop-worlds and asserts index 5 is Static Field in NONE of them (lightning_hands
in 2, nil in 4, generic_hidden in 2). So the armed leg reads damage_health_pct off an ability
that has no such key -> silent 0 (the GH #162 house rule) -> return 0, in every world.
=> zusstatic armed WITHOUT zusbind never measures the registered lever (0.09 -> ~3.45%); its
only observable effect is deleting the Static Field term (0.09 -> 0), which nobody registered.
PROMOTING zusstatic alone would ship exactly that unmeasured deletion by default -> RED.
WHY THIS IS NASTIER THAN THE pullcad TRAP: pullcad freezes a predicate FALSE, and
check_armed_wiring.py at least keeps calling it WIRED while it no-ops. Here the predicate is
TRUE on every frame -- it fires, it just answers 0 off the wrong handle. A firing gate with a
constant wrong answer looks identical to a tested-and-neutral id in every aggregate.
RELEASE CONDITION (what would retire this row): zusbind promoted, or the call site at :652
rewritten to bind Static Field by name unconditionally -- either makes the handle right
without an arm-string precondition, and then zusstatic can be judged on its own merits.

atoms.name: tower_fear_ring_disjunction
subject: towerfear
atoms.direction: one-way: promoting towerring while towerfear stays gated is NOT constrained by this row (towerring carries its own second gate at bots/mode_retreat_generic.lua:969 and stays readable).
note: THE PULLCAD TRAP IN ITS DISJUNCTIVE FORM. The halving gate is a DISJUNCTION --
`(J.IsSoakCandidate('towerfear') or J.IsSoakCandidate('towerring')) and J.IsModeTurbo()`
at bots/mode_retreat_generic.lua:964. Promoting towerfear means deleting that line, after
which the branch is turbo-default-on and arming `towerring` moves NOTHING on it -- while
check_armed_wiring.py still calls towerring WIRED, because it checks that a call site exists,
not that the predicate can still change an answer. The verdict would then read back
'tested, no effect' with nothing raising a hand: verbatim the shape AGENTS.md records for
`pullcad`, one boolean operator over.
REGISTERED THE DAY THE CONSTRAINT WAS RULED, not the day it was about to be violated --
and deliberately registered even though towerfear was WITHDRAWN from the armed set in the
same round (§FO.4): withdrawal removes the id from the string, it does not remove the gate
from bots/, so a future re-admission and promote would meet exactly this trap.
RELEASE CONDITION: promote the PAIR together (that is the configuration GH #558 proposes and
the one a wave would have to measure), or rewrite :964 so the promoted half no longer
swallows towerring's arm. Either retires this row; deleting it to get green does not.
